contributions.statement: Do not treat an agent's self-assessment of compliance or privacy NFRs plus a reviewer's 'looks right' as verification, since reviewers agreed with 91-94% of agent assessments whose satisfaction-level F1 against expert ground truth was only 0.38.
contributions.evidence: §4.1 Fig. 3/Table 5 agreement 91-94%; Table 4 satisfaction F1 0.381 (chance 0.25 assumes uniform labels). Audit: participants were Prolific crowd-workers without HIPAA expertise, one model, one Java EHR (iTrust).

contributions.statement: In spec-driven workflows, do not trust agent-produced requirement-to-code location links (code-location F1 about 0.2 on a Java codebase); require file:line citations that a deterministic check or a test referencing the requirement id confirms.
contributions.evidence: Table 4: code-location precision 0.151, recall 0.142, F1 0.203 (internally inconsistent averaging, review); 148 HIPAA-derived NFRs on iTrust; ground truth by one expert reviewed by a second.

reason: Java plus compliance evidence that convincing agent NFR assessments are mostly wrong and get rubber-stamped, and that agent trace links are unreliable; both bear directly on spec-driven rollout.
